text: Georgia’s election-interference racketeering case against President Trump was dismissed in full after prosecutors requested termination due to feasibility, legitimacy, and resource constraints. The ruling exposed collapse across prosecutorial continuity, judicial viability, and state–federal authority, while the Supreme Court’s expanded presidential immunity rendered further pursuit structurally impossible. The case’s reversal from high-risk threat to procedural dead-end created a clear inversion between substantive allegations and practical enforceability. This event expresses collapse, legitimacy, authority-split, exposure, inversion, and signal vectors as the governance layer joins the ongoing pre–Cycle-8 compression sequence.
